MAX(Y.FREE_BYTES), :"SYS_B_40")) / SUM(Y.BYTES) * :"SYS_B_41" END, :"SYS_B_42") AS USED_FILE_PCT, ROUND(CASE SUM(Y.MAX_BYTES) WHEN :"SYS_B_43" THEN :"SYS_B_44" ELSE (NVL(SUM(Y.BYTES) - MAX(Y.FREE_BYTES), :"SYS_B_45")) / SUM(Y.MAX_BYTES) * :"SYS_B_46" END, :"SYS_B_47") AS USED_FROM_MAX_PCT, CASE Y.STATUS WHEN :"SYS_B_48" THEN :"SYS_B_49" WHEN :"SYS_B_50" THEN :"SYS_B_51" WHEN :"SYS_B_52" THEN :"SYS_B_53" ELSE :"SYS_B_54" END AS STATUS FROM (SELECT ct.CON$NAME AS CON_NAME, ctf.TABLESPACE_NAME AS NAME, ct.CONTENTS, ctf.STATUS AS STATUS, ctf.BYTES AS BYTES, (SELECT ((f.TOTAL_BLOCKS - Top SQL with Top Events

  • Top SQL statements by DB Time along with the top events by DB Time for those SQLs.
  • % Activity is the percentage of DB Time due to the SQL.
  • % Event is the percentage of DB Time due to the event that the SQL is waiting on.
  • % Row Source is the percentage of DB Time due to the row source for the SQL waiting on the event.
  • Executions is the number of executions of the SQL that were sampled in ASH.

          Findings and Recommendations
          ----------------------------

Finding 1: Session Connect and Disconnect
Impact is .53 active sessions, 17.04% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Session connect and disconnect calls were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .53 active sessions, 17.04% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic for possible reduction of connect and
      disconnect calls. For example, you might use a connection pool scheme in
      the middle tier.


Finding 2: Top SQL Statements
Impact is .49 active sessions, 15.6% of total activity.

SQL statements consuming significant database time were found. These
statements offer a good opportunity for performance improvement.

Finding 3: Hard Parse
Impact is .47 active sessions, 15.12% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
Hard parsing SQL statements that encountered parse errors was not consuming
significant database time.

   No recommendations are available.


Finding 4: Soft Parse
Impact is .29 active sessions, 9.16% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .29 active sessions, 9.16% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .29 active sessions, 9.16% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.


Finding 5: Hard Parse Due to Invalidations
Impact is .19 active sessions, 6.05% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
Cursors were getting invalidated due to DDL operations. This resulted in
additional hard parses which were consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .19 active sessions, 6.05% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate appropriateness of DDL operations.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .47 active sessions, 15.12% of total activity.


Finding 6: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .07 active sessions, 2.27% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .07 active sessions, 2.27% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .47 active sessions, 15.12% of total activity.


Finding 7: Undersized SGA
Impact is .04 active sessions, 1.18% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
The SGA was inadequately sized, causing additional I/O or hard parses.
The value of parameter "sga_target" was "133120 M" during the analysis period.

   Recommendation 1: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .01 active sessions, .21% of total activity.
   -----------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Increase the size of the SGA by setting the parameter "sga_target" to
      141440 M.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .47 active sessions, 15.12% of total activity.

Finding 3: Soft Parse
Impact is .31 active sessions, 10.03% of total activity.
--------------------------------------------------------
Soft parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .31 active sessions, 10.03% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Investigate application logic to keep open the frequently used cursors.
      Note that cursors are closed by both cursor close calls and session
      disconnects.

   Recommendation 2: Database Configuration
   Estimated benefit is .31 active sessions, 10.03% of total activity.
   -------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Consider increasing the session cursor cache size by increasing the
      value of parameter "session_cached_cursors".
   Rationale
      The value of parameter "session_cached_cursors" was "500" during the
      analysis period.

Finding 6: Hard Parse Due to Sharing Criteria
Impact is .07 active sessions, 2.36% of total activity.
-------------------------------------------------------
SQL statements with the same text were not shared because of cursor
environment mismatch. This resulted in additional hard parses which were
consuming significant database time.
Common causes of environment mismatch are session NLS settings, SQL trace
settings and optimizer parameters.

   Recommendation 1: Application Analysis
   Estimated benefit is .07 active sessions, 2.36% of total activity.
   ------------------------------------------------------------------
   Action
      Look for top reason for cursor environment mismatch in
      V$SQL_SHARED_CURSOR.

   Symptoms That Led to the Finding:
   ---------------------------------
      Hard parsing of SQL statements was consuming significant database time.
      Impact is .49 active sessions, 15.74% of total activity.
